t.6.106.1: Having heard these auspicious words spoken by the Grandsire, Vibhāvasu, the god of fire, rose up, taking Vaidehī upon his lap.
t.6.106.2: She resembled the newly risen sun, adorned with ornaments of refined gold, clad in red garments, a young woman with dark, curling hair.
t.6.106.3: Taking her upon his lap, Vibhāvasu, the Fire-god, gave to Rāma the high-minded Vaidehī, unchanged in her beauty, her garlands and ornaments unwithered.
t.6.106.4: And then Pāvaka, the witness of the world, said to Rāma: "Here is your Vaidehī, O Rāma; no sin is found in her."
t.6.106.5: Neither by word, nor by mind, nor by brooding thought, nor by glance has she, virtuous and proud in her good conduct, ever been unfaithful to you.
t.6.106.6: She was carried off from the lonely forest by Rāvaṇa, that rākṣasa swollen with pride in his prowess, while she was separated from you, wretched and helpless.
t.6.106.7: Confined and closely guarded within the inner apartments, her mind fixed on you and you her sole refuge, she was watched over by hosts of deformed rākṣasīs, terrible to behold.
t.6.106.8: Though tempted in various ways and threatened as well, Maithilī gave no thought to that rākṣasa, her inmost soul being fixed on you.
t.6.106.9: Take her back, O Rāghava, she whose heart is wholly pure and who is free of sin. Nothing at all is to be said to her; I command you.
t.6.106.10: Thus addressed, Rāma, of great splendor, steadfast and firm in valor, the best of those who uphold dharma, spoke to the foremost of the thirty gods.
t.6.106.11: Surely, in the eyes of the three worlds, Sītā must undergo purification, for this auspicious lady has dwelt a long time in the inner apartments of Rāvaṇa.
t.6.106.12: "Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, is surely a fool, a man ruled by desire," so the virtuous will say of me if I take back Jānakī without first having her purified.
t.6.106.13: I too know that Maithilī, the daughter of Janaka, is devoted to me, her heart given to no other, and that she ever guards my mind.
t.6.106.14: But for the sake of the conviction of the three worlds, I, whose refuge is truth, overlooked even Vaidehī as she entered the fire.
t.6.106.15: Rāvaṇa could not have violated even this large-eyed lady, protected as she was by her own splendour, just as the great ocean does not overstep its shore.
t.6.106.16: For that evil-souled one was not able to violate Maithilī even in his mind, unattainable as she was, like a blazing tongue of fire.
t.6.106.18: Maithilī, the daughter of Janaka, is pure in all three worlds; she cannot be abandoned, just as glory cannot be cast aside by one who is self-possessed.
t.6.106.17: This auspicious lady does not deserve to be held under the dominion of Rāvaṇa's inner apartments, for Sītā is inseparable from me, just as radiance is from the sun.
t.6.106.19: And I must certainly carry out the beneficial words of all of you, who are affectionate, honoured by the world, and who speak what is beneficial in this way.
t.6.106.20: Having spoken these words, Rāma Rāghava of great strength, praised by the mighty ones for the deed he had accomplished by his own hand, was reunited with his beloved, and he who was worthy of happiness experienced happiness.
